n: Sanctions Evasion via Shell and Ownership Layering (50% Rule Circumvention)
ds: Designated persons may retain control of assets by reducing recorded ownership below aggregation thresholds, using nominees, trusts, family members or layered holding companies. Detection depends on ownership and control analysis that looks beyond percentage holdings to influence, funding and benefit.

src.t: OFAC, Guidance on Entities Owned by Persons Whose Property and Interests in Property Are Blocked (50 Percent Rule) (2014)
OFSI, UK Financial Sanctions General Guidance (ownership and control section)
FATF, Guidance on Beneficial Ownership of Legal Persons (2023)

cn.rt: Nominee or relative holds accounts for a designated person; consumer accounts opened digitally or in branch can act as fronts, though corporate layering is out of scope.

rat: Designated persons holding control via nominees, relatives and layered holding companies; exposed at onboarding and ownership screening.

ind.n: Recent ownership reductions by a designated person around designation date
ind.cx: Shareholdings are transferred or diluted shortly before or after a designation, often to relatives or associates.
ind.fp: Genuine succession planning or restructuring can coincide.
ind.ds: Shareholdings are transferred or diluted shortly before or after a designation, often to relatives or associates.

ind.n: Aggregate designated-party ownership just below the threshold
ind.cx: Several designated parties each hold stakes that together reach but are individually below the threshold, or holdings sit at just under the limit.
ind.fp: Minority stakes are routine in investments.
ind.ds: Several designated parties each hold stakes that together reach but are individually below the threshold, or holdings sit at just under the limit.

ind.n: Nominee shareholders, directors or trustees with limited independent role
ind.cx: Registered officers appear to act on instruction, serve many entities or have no business connection.
ind.fp: Professional nominees are lawful in many jurisdictions.
ind.ds: Registered directors or shareholders appear to act for undisclosed principals, serve many entities or have no real decision-making role.

ind.n: Family members or close associates acquiring assets and positions
ind.cx: Relatives or known associates assume ownership or management of designated person's holdings.
ind.fp: Family businesses commonly pass to relatives.
ind.ds: Relatives or known associates assume ownership or management of designated person's holdings.

ind.n: Complex multi-jurisdiction holding chain without economic rationale
ind.cx: Layers across secrecy-prone jurisdictions with trusts or foundations and no clear commercial purpose.
ind.fp: Tax and legal planning can be legitimate.
ind.ds: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.
ind.cn: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale

ind.n: Funding of a company by a designated person's connected sources
ind.cx: Capital injections, loans or guarantees come from entities linked to a designated party.
ind.ds: Capital injections, loans or guarantees come from entities linked to a designated party.

ind.n: Customer unwilling or unable to explain ownership or control
ind.cx: Evasive, delayed or inconsistent explanations about owners, controllers or purpose.
ind.fp: Complex family businesses can take time to document.
ind.ds: Customer or intermediary is vague, delayed or inconsistent when asked who owns, controls or ultimately benefits from an account, entity or funds.
ind.cn: Reluctance to disclose beneficial ownership or control

ind.n: Shared addresses, phone numbers or advisers with designated entities
ind.cx: Entities share contact details, advisers or bank accounts with designated persons.
ind.ds: Entities share contact details, advisers or bank accounts with designated persons.

ctl.ds: Aggregates holdings of all designated persons, tests who really controls an entity despite formal shareholdings, and reviews recent ownership transfers and threshold proximity. It prevents ownership-based sanctions thresholds being avoided by splitting or nominee transfers.

Re-screens the customer base, linked parties and counterparties whenever sanctions or other lists change and on trigger events, with prompt list synchronisation. It closes the gap between onboarding checks and later designations.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Requires nominee shareholders, directors and signatories to declare their status and name the person they act for, and declines or immobilises bearer instruments. It limits the use of nominees and bearer forms to conceal the real controller.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

ctl.n: PEP, relative and close associate screening
ctl.ds: Screens customers, beneficial owners, controllers, counterparties and their relatives and close associates against politically exposed person data at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Matches trigger enhanced measures and senior approval.

Requires a documented commercial or legal reason for each layer of a multi-tier or cross-border structure, with specialist review and sign-off before approval. Unexplained complexity is treated as a risk driver and can lead to decline.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

Prevents account opening or activity until ownership and control information is provided and verified, with refusals escalated to compliance and unresolved cases handled under a defined policy. It stops relationships starting on withheld or unresolved ownership.

Routes potential sanctions, proscription or restricted-party exposure to a specialist sanctions or legal team for decision before proceeding, and sets conditions for finance and insurance. It ensures complex legal judgements are made by qualified people.

Briefs front-line, onboarding and investigation staff on current red flags, typologies and escalation routes, including sector-specific patterns and professional-enabler behaviours. It improves recognition of suspicious activity that rules alone cannot see.
